request.system:
You are the extractor in Ledger, a system that documents legacy COBOL business rules so that a modern port can be written from the rules alone and checked against the running original.

Write business rules as Given/When/Then scenarios in plain English that a policy owner can read and approve. Hard requirements:

- Every clause cites the exact source lines it comes from (file plus [first, last] line numbers from the numbered listing; keep spans tight, normally 1-12 lines). If a statement cannot be sourced to specific lines, leave it out.
- Every clause lists the COBOL data names ("fields") and literal values ("literals": codes, messages, constants, without quotes) it relies on. Each listed field and literal must literally appear in the cited lines; a checker will reject the clause otherwise. Cite a declaration line (for example a PIC clause in WORKING-STORAGE) when the clause depends on a field's size or precision.
- Describe what the code actually does, not what it was probably meant to do. If the code has surprising behaviour (a later check overwriting an earlier result, a branch that can never run, arithmetic that truncates, a check that ignores something), state that behaviour precisely in the rule.
- Separate business logic from file plumbing. Opening/closing files, file-status checks, and abend handling are plumbing; leave them out unless they change a business outcome. Balance and record updates (for example 2700-*, 2800-*, 1050-* paragraphs) are business logic: a port that skips them would produce different output files.
- Be precise enough that a developer who never sees the COBOL could reproduce the outputs exactly: name the output fields set, the exact codes and message texts, the order of checks, signs and arithmetic (COBOL truncates toward zero unless ROUNDED is written), and which records are created versus updated.
- Keep each clause to one checkable fact. When a fact depends on a record layout, field size or precision, put it in its own clause that cites the declaration. Do not restate in one clause what another clause (or another part of the program) establishes.
- Use the field names exactly as declared. Use the tools to read any other paragraph or field layout you need; do not guess line numbers.

Return only rules for the unit you are given, at most the number requested, each one a distinct behaviour with an observable effect on the program's outputs.

Program: CBACT04C (CBACT04C.cbl, 653 lines). Copybooks: CVTRA01Y, CVACT03Y, CVTRA02Y, CVACT01Y, CVTRA05Y.

Unit: CBACT04C-main. Focus: The top-level loop over category balance records grouped by account, and when and how each account record is updated with accumulated interest. Rate lookup and the interest computation itself are covered by other units.
Return at most 2 rule(s).

Files (FILE-CONTROL):
  TCATBAL-FILE: ASSIGN TCATBALF, INDEXED SEQUENTIAL, key FD-TRAN-CAT-KEY
  XREF-FILE: ASSIGN XREFFILE, INDEXED RANDOM, key FD-XREF-CARD-NUM, alternate key FD-XREF-ACCT-ID
  ACCOUNT-FILE: ASSIGN ACCTFILE, INDEXED RANDOM, key FD-ACCT-ID
  DISCGRP-FILE: ASSIGN DISCGRP, INDEXED RANDOM, key FD-DISCGRP-KEY
  TRANSACT-FILE: ASSIGN TRANSACT, SEQUENTIAL SEQUENTIAL, key None

content.text: {"rules":[{"title":"Account balance update when the account number changes","paragraph":"(main)","summary":"Category balance records are processed in key order and grouped by consecutive account ID. When a record's account ID differs from the previous one, and this is not the first record, the previous account is updated before the new account is loaded. The update adds the group's total interest to the current balance, sets the cycle credit and debit to zero and rewrites the account record.","given":[{"text":"At program start, the first-record flag WS-FIRST-TIME is 'Y'.","file":"CBACT04C.cbl","lines":[170,170],"fields":["WS-FIRST-TIME"],"literals":["Y"]},{"text":"At program start, the last-seen account number WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM is spaces, so the first record always looks like a new account.","file":"CBACT04C.cbl","lines":[167,167],"fields":["WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM"],"literals":[]},{"text":"Category balance records are read one at a time in key order from TCATBAL-FILE into TRAN-CAT-BAL-RECORD. Grouping depends only on consecutive records having the same account ID.","file":"CBACT04C.cbl","lines":[326,326],"fields":["TRAN-CAT-BAL-RECORD"],"literals":[]},{"text":"Interest is computed for a category balance record, and added to the group total, only when the looked-up rate DIS-INT-RATE is not zero.","file":"CBACT04C.cbl","lines":[213,217],"fields":["DIS-INT-RATE"],"literals":[]},{"text":"Each computed monthly interest amount is added to the running account total WS-TOTAL-INT.","file":"CBACT04C.cbl","lines":[467,467],"fields":["WS-MONTHLY-INT","WS-TOTAL-INT"],"literals":[]}],"when":[{"text":"A category balance record is read whose TRANCAT-ACCT-ID differs from WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM, and WS-FIRST-TIME is not 'Y'.","file":"CBACT04C.cbl","lines":[194,196],"fields":["TRANCAT-ACCT-ID","WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM","WS-FIRST-TIME"],"literals":["Y"]}],"then":[{"text":"The account update runs before the new account is read. As a result, ACCOUNT-RECORD still holds the previous account when it is updated.","file":"CBACT04C.cbl","lines":[196,203],"fields":["FD-ACCT-ID","TRANCAT-ACCT-ID"],"literals":[]},{"text":"The previous account's current balance ACCT-CURR-BAL is increased by WS-TOTAL-INT (an add with no rounding). This happens even when the total is zero because every category had a zero rate.","file":"CBACT04C.cbl","lines":[350,352],"fields":["WS-TOTAL-INT","ACCT-CURR-BAL"],"literals":[]},{"text":"ACCT-CURR-BAL holds 10 integer digits and 2 decimals, signed.","file":"CVACT01Y.cpy","lines":[7,7],"fields":["ACCT-CURR-BAL"],"literals":[]},{"text":"WS-TOTAL-INT holds 9 integer digits and 2 decimals, signed.","file":"CBACT04C.cbl","lines":[169,169],"fields":["WS-TOTAL-INT"],"literals":[]},{"text":"The previous account's current-cycle credit ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT and current-cycle debit ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT are both set to zero.","file":"CBACT04C.cbl","lines":[353,354],"fields":["ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT","ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT"],"literals":[]},{"text":"The account record is rewritten in place from ACCOUNT-RECORD. All other account fields keep the values that were read.","file":"CBACT04C.cbl","lines":[356,356],"fields":["FD-ACCTFILE-REC","ACCOUNT-RECORD"],"literals":[]},{"text":"On the very first record, no update is done. Instead, WS-FIRST-TIME is set to 'N'.","file":"CBACT04C.cbl","lines":[197,199],"fields":["WS-FIRST-TIME"],"literals":["N"]},{"text":"In both cases, WS-TOTAL-INT is reset to 0 and WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM is set to the new TRANCAT-ACCT-ID.","file":"CBACT04C.cbl","lines":[200,201],"fields":["WS-TOTAL-INT","WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM","TRANCAT-ACCT-ID"],"literals":[]},{"text":"The new account is read from the account file by TRANCAT-ACCT-ID. Its card cross-reference is read by the alternate key FD-XREF-ACCT-ID.","file":"CBACT04C.cbl","lines":[202,205],"fields":["TRANCAT-ACCT-ID","FD-ACCT-ID","FD-XREF-ACCT-ID"],"literals":[]}]},{"title":"The last account group is never written back at end of file","paragraph":"(main)","summary":"The end-of-file branch that should update the last account (ELSE PERFORM 1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT) can never run. The loop condition is tested before each pass, so the loop ends as soon as END-OF-FILE becomes 'Y'. The last account in the category balance file therefore never gets its interest added or its cycle credit and debit zeroed, but its interest transactions are still written.","given":[{"text":"END-OF-FILE starts as 'N'.","file":"CBACT04C.cbl","lines":[137,137],"fields":["END-OF-FILE"],"literals":["N"]},{"text":"The main loop repeats until END-OF-FILE = 'Y', and the test is made before each pass. Inside the loop, the ELSE branch that performs the account update is taken only when END-OF-FILE is not 'N' at the top of a pass.","file":"CBACT04C.cbl","lines":[188,191],"fields":["END-OF-FILE"],"literals":["Y","N"]},{"text":"The ELSE branch would perform the account update.","file":"CBACT04C.cbl","lines":[219,222],"fields":[],"literals":[]},{"text":"For each record of the last account with a non-zero rate, interest is computed and an interest transaction is written during the loop.","file":"CBACT04C.cbl","lines":[214,217],"fields":["DIS-INT-RATE"],"literals":[]}],"when":[{"text":"Reading the category balance file returns status '10' (end of file), which sets APPL-RESULT to 16.","file":"CBACT04C.cbl","lines":[330,331],"fields":["TCATBALF-STATUS","APPL-RESULT"],"literals":["10","16"]},{"text":"APPL-EOF (APPL-RESULT value 16) causes END-OF-FILE to be set to 'Y'.","file":"CBACT04C.cbl","lines":[339,340],"fields":["END-OF-FILE"],"literals":["Y"]}],"then":[{"text":"The inner check END-OF-FILE = 'N' is now false, so nothing more is done in that pass. The loop then stops at its next test, so the ELSE branch's account update never runs.","file":"CBACT04C.cbl","lines":[191,191],"fields":["END-OF-FILE"],"literals":["N"]},{"text":"As a result, the last account group's WS-TOTAL-INT is never added to ACCT-CURR-BAL, its cycle credit and debit are not zeroed, and its account record is not rewritten. If the file is empty, no account is updated at all.","file":"CBACT04C.cbl","lines":[352,356],"fields":["WS-TOTAL-INT","ACCT-CURR-BAL","ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT","ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT"],"literals":[]}]}]}
